body: System information (version)  OpenVINO => 2020.4.689 Operating System / Platform => Windows 10 64 Bit Compiler => Visual Studio 2019 Problem classification: model execution with ONNX Runtime Framework: PyTorch / ONNX Model name: A single-layered model ONNX Runtime with OpenVino Execution Provider support was cloned from https://github.com/intel/onnxruntime, with tag v3.1, and built locally. Hardware: Neural Compute Stick 2  Detailed description Seems that Conv3d gets executed on the CPU despite all my efforts to force execution on the Myriad VPU. To confirm this, I ran a model composed of Conv3d only, when the compute stick was disconnected, and (to my surprise) got valid results. Steps to reproduce I used the following code snippet: import numpy as np import onnx import onnxruntime as ort import torch.onnx import torch.nn as nn  def run_model(conv_type, use_myriad):      if conv_type == 'conv2d':         x = torch.ones((4, 64, 100, 100))         instance = nn.Conv2d(             in_channels=64,             out_channels=64,             kernel_size=3,         )      elif conv_type == 'conv3d':         x = torch.ones((4, 1, 27, 15, 15))         instance = nn.Conv3d(                 in_channels=1,                 out_channels=64,                 kernel_size=(3, 3, 3),                 bias=False,                 stride=(1, 2, 2),                 padding=0             )     else:         raise 'what?'      instance.eval()      scripted_cell = torch.jit.script(instance)      torch_result = instance(x)     scripted_result = scripted_cell(x)      np.testing.assert_almost_equal(torch_result.detach().numpy(), scripted_result.detach().numpy(), 4)      torch.onnx.export(         model=scripted_cell,         args=(x,),         f='net.onnx',         # verbose=True,         input_names=['x'],         output_names=['result'],         example_outputs=torch_result,         opset_version=13,         dynamic_axes={             'x': {0: 'batch_size'},         },     )      # Load the ONNX model     model = onnx.load("net.onnx")      # Check that the model is well formed     onnx.checker.check_model(model)      if use_myriad:         ort_session = ort.InferenceSession("net.onnx",             providers=['OpenVINOExecutionProvider'],             provider_options=[{'device_type': 'MYRIAD_FP16'}]         )     else:         ort_session = ort.InferenceSession("net.onnx")      outputs = ort_session.run(None, {'x': x.detach().numpy()})     onnx_result = outputs[0]      np.testing.assert_almost_equal(onnx_result, scripted_result.detach().numpy(), 4)      print('OK')  I then disconnected my compute stick, and invoked: >>> run_model('conv2d', use_myriad=False) OK >>> run_model('conv3d', use_myriad=False) OK  That's as expected, as the models ran on the CPU. And then, while the compute stick is still disconnected I ran: >>> run_model('conv3d', use_myriad=True) OK # <<<< this should have been an error, such as the one below >>> run_model('conv2d', use_myriad=True) 2021-10-14 18:18:13.9225885 [E:onnxruntime:, sequential_executor.cc:339 onnxruntime::SequentialExecutor::Execute] Non-zero status code returned while running OpenVINO-EP-subgraph_14 node. body: System information (version)  OpenVINO=> 2020.4 Operating System / Platform => Windows 64 Bit Compiler => Visual Studio 2019 Framework => TensorFlow  I successfully converted saved_model.pb to IR file by model optimizer, but encountered an error as followed: exec_net = ie.load_network(network=self.net, device_name='CPU') File "ie_api.pyx", line 372, in openvino.inference_engine.ie_api.IECore.load_network File "ie_api.pyx", line 390, in openvino.inference_engine.ie_api.IECore.load_network RuntimeError: Ngraph operation NonZero with name StatefulPartitionedCall/model/tf_op_layer_Where/Where/NonZero_ has dynamic output shape on 0 port, but CPU plug-in supports only static shape  The xml file: <layer id="916" name="StatefulPartitionedCall/model/tf_op_layer_Where/Where/NonZero_" type="NonZero" version="opset3"> 	<data output_type="i64"/> 	<input> 		<port id="0" precision="BOOL"> 			<dim>10647</dim> 		</port> 	</input> 	<output> 		<port id="1" precision="I64"> 			<dim>1</dim> 			<dim>10647</dim> 		</port> 	</output> </layer>   Steps to reproduce I trained a yolov3 model on a custom dataset, and converted this Tensorflow model to IR file by followed command: python "C:\Program Files (x86)\Intel\openvino_2021.4.689\deployment_tools\model_optimizer\mo_tf.py" --saved_model_dir=YOLO --output_dir=. --input_shape=[1,416,416,3]

title: [Bug] Failed to convert TensorFlow saved model with LayerNormalization
author: wangg
body: System information (version)  OpenVINO: 2021.4.689 Operating System / Platform: Ubuntu 20.04 (x86) Compiler: gcc version 9.3.0 Problem classification: Model Conversion Framework: TensorFlow  Detailed description Cannot convert Tensorflow models with LayerNormalization layer. Steps to reproduce  Create saved model from Tensorflow 2.4.1  from tensorflow import keras  model = keras.Sequential([     keras.layers.Input(shape=(224, 224, 3), batch_size=1),     keras.layers.LayerNormalization(),     keras.layers.Activation("relu"), ])  model.save("ln_saved_model")  Convert TensorFlow saved model to OpenVINO IR  mo.py --framework tf --saved_model_dir ln_saved_model Error message: [ ERROR ]  Exception occurred during running replacer "fusing" (<class 'extensions.middle.fusings.Fusing'>): After partial shape inference were found shape collision for node StatefulPartitionedCall/sequential/layer_normalization/FusedBatchNormV3/beta (old shape: [    1 50176     3     1], new shape: [    1 50176     3 50176])  Issue submission checklist   I report the issue, it's not a question  I checked the problem with documentation, FAQ, open issues, Stack Overflow, etc and have not found solution  There is reproducer code and related data files: images, videos, models, etc.

title: [Bug] cpu_throughput_streams from 1 to 2 or other positive number（>1）openvino can't load the model
author: duhuajiang
body: OpenVINO = 2021.4 Operating System / Platform = linux when I set the cpu_throughput_streams=1, openvino can load the model and run, and get the right result, but when I change the cpu_throughput_streams from 1 to  2 or other positive number（>1）,openvino can't load the model, so can't get result. the error is: mkldnn_memory.h:120  can not get the memory. so I debug into the function LoadNetwork, I find the node（Canstant -> i32{0}）,can not generate with the mkldnn_input_node. so i read the code of  MKLDNNInputNode::MKLDNNInputNode(), find the lambda exp: auto cloneBlob = [&, this] () {         MKLDNNMemory memory{ getEngine() };         memory.Create(memDesc, constOp->get_data_ptr());          MKLDNNMemoryPtr ptr = MKLDNNMemoryPtr(new MKLDNNMemory(getEngine()));         ptr->Create(memDesc);         ptr->SetData(memory);          return ptr;     };    the ptr->SetData(memory) throw the exception. because function SetData(memory), need get handle to data, but function  Create with i32{0},did not build the data, so setData error. solution: I change the lambda to: auto cloneBlob = [&, this] () {         MKLDNNMemoryPtr ptr = MKLDNNMemoryPtr(new MKLDNNMemory(getEngine()));         ptr->Create(memDesc, constOp->get_data_ptr());         return ptr;     };    so  the vino can load model and run, get the right results.

title: Model with different result when running with Myriad [Bug]
author: PCPJ
body: System information (version)  OpenVINO => Operating System / Platform => Ubuntu 20.04.3 LTS, running inside a docker container (that is being hosted by a Ubuntu 20.04.3 LTS) Problem classification: Model Conversion Framework: PyTorch Model name: MobileNet_v2 (with some modifications)  Detailed description I have two multi-label classification models, A and B, that I trained by myself. Model A is performing much better than model B. The problem I am facing is that both models are losing precision when I ran at the Myriad (I am using a Luxonis OAK-1-PCBA). With losing precision I mean: running the same model at the same input image with different hardware (nvidia-gpu, intel-cpu, and Myriad) and receiving output scores that aren't the same. This loss of precision is relevant at model B, and is huge at model A. Here are the scores I received from model A and B at the same image with 4 different hardware: Model A - Nvidia (using pytorch)  Model A - CPU (using the model converted to xml and the OpenVino Engine)  Model A - Myriad (using the model converted to xml and the OpenVIno Engine)  Model A - Myriad (using the model converted to blob and the Luxonis API)  Model B - Nvidia (using pytorch)  Model B - CPU (using the model converted to xml and the OpenVino Engine)  Model B - Myriad (using the model converted to xml and the OpenVino Engine)  Model B - Myriad (using the model converted to blob and the Luxonis API)  Steps to reproduce I am sharing the python class I am using to generate the results with the OpenVino engine. Also sharing the models converted to IR (xml/bin) and to blob. Gogle drive link The commands I am using to convert the models are: python3 mo.py --input_model ModelA.onnx --input_shape [1,3,480,640] --data_type=FP16 --scale_values=[58.395,57.120,57.375] --mean_values=[123.675,116.28,103.53] --reverse_input_channels --move_to_preprocess --disable_fusing --disable_resnet_optimization  ./myriad_compile -m ModelA.xml -ip U8 -VPU_NUMBER_OF_SHAVES 6 -VPU_NUMBER_OF_CMX_SLICES 6  The reason I am using the last parameters at the mo.py is to test if it would reduce the difference in the results. It didn't. I converted the pytorch model to ONNX already using half precision, and the test running at the Nvidia-gpu used 16bits float numbers. author: KodeWorker
body: System information (version)  OpenVINO => 2021.4.752 Operating System / Platform => Windows 64 Bit Compiler => Visual Studio 2022 Problem classification: Model Conversion Framework: ONNX (from tf2onnx) Model name: Deeplab V3+  Detailed description Inconsistant values while converting ONNX model to OpenVINO IR. The values in the layer, resize_2/ResizeBilinear, is almost the same for both ONNX model and OpenVINO IR. But the next layer (Softmax:0) in ONNX model is converted into serveral layers in OpenVINO IR. We got incorrect values in the OpenVINO.  ONNX model link: GoogleDrive Converted IR model link:  GoogleDrive  In the ONNX model, the Softmax layer will do softmax along the last axis (axis=-1 by default) ONNX Softmax Description  In the OpenVINO IR (xml), the input shape (1x512x512x2) will be flatten (1x524288) and then do the softmax. This results in very small values in the output layer, and the operation is innconsistent with Softmax in ONNX model.  Are there any pointers to fix this problem? title: FakeQuantize layer, from IR to IE
author: piti-diablotin
body: System information (version)  OpenVINO => 2021.4 Operating System / Platform => docker openvino_data_dev Problem classification: Quantization  Detailed description I'm currently trying to implement a new algorithm to quantize an IR model. I'm working in the pot.py utility tool. I created a new quantization algorithm which is found and launched correctly. I got an IR in the xml format which seems very fine. The problem is that the inference is done in float32 and not int8 despite the addition of FakeQuantize layers (checked with DLWorkbench runtine precision). The diff.tar.gz archive contains 2 xml files of IR models. It seems to me that they are very similar in architecture, the offset attribute for Const layers are different but size are the same and the graphs contain the same layers. The DefaultQuantization xml IR is correctly inferred in int8 and has a good performance increase (2 times more FPS) however the EdQuant (my implementation) has not. It is as slow as with float32 model or even worse sometimes due to FQ overhead. Currently my implementation does not do anything, it fills the parameters of the FakeQuantize layers with positive random numbers around 0 for low input/output and around 250 for high input/output with 256 levels. I plan to correctly set the bounds later on when I get a model that runs in int8, but maybe that's a bad idea ? How FQ layer bounds affect the IE to infer in low precision int8 ? I'm looking for any help on the requirements for the IE to indeed infer with low precision int8 numbers. All my tests are performed on CPU only (target device) and tested on i7-1185G7 and Xeon Gold 6258 both with AVX-512 AVX-512VNNI and DLBoost Thanks for any help you can provide !

title: [Bug] ONNX model after convertation doesn't work on AMD
author: IlyaDobrynin
body: System information (version)   OpenVINO=> 2020.3 Operating System / Platform => Ubuntu 18.04 Problem classification => Model Conversion Framework: PyTorch  Detailed description There is a strange bug in ONNX to OpenVino convertation of my model. I use OSNet and make this steps of convertations:  PyTorch -> ONNX ONNX -> OpenVino  The model has a LightConv3x3 layer. In this layer nn.Conv2d with kernel size 3 and number of groups == number of output_channels follows nn.Conv2d with kernel size 1. This sequence of layers after ONNX -> OpenVino convertation doesn't work on AMD processor (I have tested on Ryzen 3950x), despite the fact that on the Intel CPU everything works fine. "Does not work" means "return random values". After long and quite painful debugging process I have investigated that sequence [group-Conv2d 3x3 -> Conv2d 1x1] - simply swap layers - works perfectly on both AMD and Intel. Suppose this is a bug. Steps to reproduce Note: I use model-optimizer/mo_onnx.py with flags: --disable_resnet_optimization --disable_weights_compression --disable_fusing --disable_gfusing Does not work on AMD: class LightConv3x3(nn.Module):     def __init__(self, in_channels, out_channels):         super(LightConv3x3, self).__init__()         self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(in_channels, out_channels, 1, stride=1, padding=0, bias=False)         self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(out_channels, out_channels, 3, stride=1, padding=1, bias=False, groups=out_channels)         self.bn = nn.BatchNorm2d(out_channels)         self.relu = nn.ReLU(inplace=True)      def forward(self, x):         x = self.conv1(x)         x = self.conv2(x)         x = self.bn(x)         return self.relu(x)  But this code works fine: class LightConv3x3(nn.Module):     def __init__(self, in_channels, out_channels):         super(LightConv3x3, self).__init__()         self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(in_channels, in_channels, 3, stride=1, padding=1, bias=False, groups=in_channels)         self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(in_channels, out_channels, 1, stride=1, padding=0, bias=False)         self.bn = nn.BatchNorm2d(out_channels)         self.relu = nn.ReLU(inplace=True)      def forward(self, x):         x = self.conv1(x)         x = self.conv2(x)         x = self.bn(x)         return self.relu(x)  Issue submission checklist    I report the issue, it's not a question     I checked the problem with documentation, FAQ, open issues, Stack Overflow, etc and have not found solution      There is reproducer code and related data files: images, videos, models, etc.

title: Converting a trained model for inference but using Training=True
author: dennex
body: I have trained a Pix2Pix network using Keras Tensorflow, following this tutorial. The Pix2Pix uses Instance Normalization, such that when doing inference, we would need to have the Instance Normalization layers (batch norm for batch size of 1) to compute the sample mean and variance. In Tensorflow, I would call the forward as pred = model(x, training=True). The model is the generator part of the Pix2Pix, which is a UNet with Instance Normalization. model = tf.keras.models.load_model("pix2pix") pred = model(img, training=True)  https://www.tensorflow.org/tutorials/generative/pix2pix We are using this model in C++ using the OpenCV DNN to perform inference, and we are using OpenVINO to convert a TF "saved_model" into Intermediate Representation for being loaded by OpenCV DNN. The problem is that when doing inference, the Batch normalizations layers use the trained statistics to do normalization, whereas we would want the u and sigma to be calculated "per instance" even in inference. Is there a way to convert a saved_model into intermediate representation keeping the "training=True"?

title: Apple silicon (M1) prebuilt openvino with arm plugin wheels released on PyPI
author: cansik
body: I have created an automated script to build openvino for Apple silicon (M1) Mac (BigSur 11 and Monterey 12). The build uses the openvino-contrib arm plugin to allow networks to be run on arm64 Macs. The release is meant for developers to have an easy way to tryout native openvino on Mac M1. There are still some know issues which is why I would not recommend to use it for production (at the end of this issue). The prebuilt binaries are hosted on PyPI which makes the installation as simple as possible: pip install openvino-arm  If you want to include openvino in a requirements.txt, I would suggest the following two lines to either install the default version or the Apple silicon version: openvino>=2022.1.0; platform_system != "Darwin" and platform.machine != 'arm64' openvino-arm>=2022.1.0; platform_system == "Darwin" and platform.machine == 'arm64'  I look forward to feedback and suggestions from the community. Hopefully the official openvino wheels will be updated soon to support Apple silicon. Know Issues  It seems that at the moment only FP32 is supported and performance is not as good as on Intel machines. At the moment the build includes opencv3 binaries as well, which can lead to a version conflict warnings between the package opencv dylibs and the opencv-python installation. There is still an issue with building older numpy versions on M1. Because of that the package loosens the numpy requirement to be just >=1.16.6 as mentioned in #11532. For example numpy 1.22.3 works fine with deprecation warnings.

title: 64 bit master branch build loads model with wrong(?) parameters
author: marcjasner
body: I have created a build of OpenVINO from the master branch based on 64bit Ubuntu 20.04 that I am using for an Armbian 22.02 based system (Libre Computers Le Potato due to Raspberry Pi being harder to get at the moment). I used the RPi64 docker file and modified it to use Python 3.8.10 (as that's what's used in Armbian. Everything builds without errors. I was using some of the open_model_zoo demos as a quick test to make sure it works ok, and I ran into the following problem: When using the human_pose_estimation_demo program it loads everything successfully but does not get any pose detection results. After some debugging I traced it to an issue loading the model. When loading the human-pose-estimation-0001.xml I get the following output: [ INFO ] OpenVINO Runtime [ INFO ]        build: custom_master_54e5af95da0c4288c4c9c18410748c02715f8009 [ INFO ] Reading model /home/marc/models/omz/FP16/human-pose-estimation-0001.xml [ WARNING ] The parameter "padding_mode" not found in OpenPose wrapper, will be omitted [ WARNING ] The parameter "delta" not found in OpenPose wrapper, will be omitted [ DEBUG ]       Reshape model from [1, 3, 256, 456] to [1, 3, 256, 344] [ INFO ]        Input layer: data, shape: [1, 3, 256, 344], precision: f32, layout: NCHW [ INFO ]        Output layer: pafs, shape: [1, 38, 32, 43], precision: f32, layout: [ INFO ]        Output layer: heatmaps, shape: [1, 19, 32, 43], precision: f32, layout: [ INFO ]        Output layer: pooled_heatmaps, shape: [1, 19, 32, 57], precision: f32, layout: When tracing through the code I found all results fail because at one point the code compares heatmaps with pooled_heatmaps and that check fails because they are different shaped arrays ( [1,19,32,43] vs [1,19,32,57] ). This code works fine on my Raspberry Pi build of OpenVINO which was built from the same branch, just using the RPi32 docker file and the version of Python that Raspbian Buster uses (3.7.9). The output from the loading of the same model on the Pi shows: [ INFO ] OpenVINO Runtime [ INFO ]        build: custom_master_531fa9018d52277a4c91f3690b63382e1fc1eb94 [ INFO ] Reading model /home/pi/models/omz/FP16/human-pose-estimation-0001.xml [ WARNING ] The parameter "padding_mode" not found in OpenPose wrapper, will be omitted [ WARNING ] The parameter "delta" not found in OpenPose wrapper, will be omitted [ DEBUG ]       Reshape model from [1, 3, 256, 456] to [1, 3, 256, 344] [ INFO ]        Input layer: data, shape: [1, 3, 256, 344], precision: f32, layout: NCHW [ INFO ]        Output layer: pafs, shape: [1, 38, 32, 43], precision: f32, layout: [ INFO ]        Output layer: heatmaps, shape: [1, 19, 32, 43], precision: f32, layout: [ INFO ]        Output layer: pooled_heatmaps, shape: [1, 19, 32, 43], precision: f32, layout: You can see the pooled_heatmaps layer loads with shape [1,19,32,43], and so the comparison to heatmaps succeeds in the code. I have compared the md5sum of the model and bin files and they are identical between the two systems, so I don't see why the model loads with one shape on the 64 bit build and another shape on the 32 bit build. Can you please assist or point me in the direction of anything that might help me get to the bottom of this? Thanks in advance!

title: [Feature Request] cmake is always re-download dependencies even `ENABLE_UNSAFE_LOCATIONS` is set
author: yantaozhao
body: System information (version)   OpenVINO=> source code- master branch Operating System / Platform => Windows 10 Compiler =>  cmake3.21 + visual studio 2019 Problem classification => Issue of compiling from source code  Detailed description  When using cmake to configure the building progress, dependency files which were previous downloaded in ${SRC_ROOT}\temp\download\ will be download online again, though cmake variable ENABLE_UNSAFE_LOCATIONS is set ON, and downloaded files' sha256 match. Steps to reproduce 1, for convenient, set ie_option (ENABLE_UNSAFE_LOCATIONS "skip check for MD5 for dependency" ON) (OFF->ON)  directly in features.cmake file. 2, try to configure cd ${SRC_ROOT} cd build cmake .. // wait for success, and dependencies were downloaded in ..\temp\download\, then removed by cmake  //now do another configure cd ${SRC_ROOT} cd build2 cmake .. // files in ..\temp\download\ are re-downloading again Wanted result 1, Basically, when do the second configuration, previous downloaded files should not re-download again. 2, A more decent solution: save the downloaded files, and instead of using the checkless ENABLE_UNSAFE_LOCATIONS, we can check the sha256 to make the decision whether re-download related file or not. Some cmake snippet maybe look like this: inside cmake file, replace: if (ENABLE_UNSAFE_LOCATIONS) with: file(SHA256 ${archive_path} downloaded_archive_sha256) if (${downloaded_archive_sha256} STREQUAL ${sha256})   ... endif()  BRs.

title: [Bug] Using index to get the IE internal inputs name may get the wrong result.
author: miaobin
body: System information (version)   OpenVINO => 2021.4 Operating System / Platform => Windows 64 Bit Compiler => Visual Studio 2019 Problem classification: Graphic Compilation Model name: RNNoise  Detailed description When the model has multiple inputs, we may get wrong results by suing the IE internal input names through the ie_network_get_input_name() function. Steps to reproduce As the following code (src/bindings/c/src/ie_c_api.cpp) shows:  1 using InputsDataMap = std::map<std::string, InputInfo::Ptr>;  2  3 IEStatusCode ie_network_get_input_name(const ie_network_t *network, size_t number, char **name) {  4    if (network == nullptr || name == nullptr) {  5         return IEStatusCode::GENERAL_ERROR;  6    }  7  8    IEStatusCode status = IEStatusCode::OK;  9 10   try { 11        IE::InputsDataMap inputs = network->object.getInputsInfo(); 12 13        // check if the number is out of bounds. 14        if (number >= inputs.size()) { 15            status = IEStatusCode::OUT_OF_BOUNDS; 16        } else { 17            IE::InputsDataMap::iterator iter = inputs.begin(); 18            for (size_t i = 0; i < number; ++i) { 19                ++iter; 20            } 21            std::unique_ptr<char[]> inputName(new char[iter->first.length() + 1]); 22            *name = inputName.release(); 23            memcpy(*name, iter->first.c_str(), iter->first.length() + 1); 24        } 25    } CATCH_IE_EXCEPTIONS 26 27    return status; 28 }  InputsDataMap is a map that contains string as key, and InputInfo smart pointer as value. As a map, all elements are automatically sorted by key value. So InputsDataMap will be sorted according to string automatically. And this is the key that will causes getting the wrong IE internal input name from the index. For example, A model has three inputs and there IE internal input names are: parameter_0, parameter_8, parameter_12. The order we need is (0, 1, 2), but with the above function we will get an input in the order (0, 2, 1). title: Compile-time fallback for missing plugins.xml
author: CSBVision
body: Hello, we recently started using OpenVINO as a backend for OpenCV's DNN module. As we only need a relatively small selection of features for this purpose (only the Intel CPU plugin as well as the Inference Engine frontend), we compiled OpenVINO ourselves. We prefer using OpenVINO as shared libraries and everything works fine. Still, the shared libraries depend on the plugins.xml configuration file at runtime. As this is redundant here - the desired configuration is already known at compile time - but also yields a runtime error if missing, we would like to propose to add a compile-time fallback for a missing plugins.xml, similar to the static library case. By investigating how the plugin registration works in the static library case, we found the getStaticPluginsRegistry() function in ie_plugins.hpp that is generated by the plugins.cmake script. Here, we think that similarly generating the file by CMake should also be possible in the dynamic library case such that while calling Core::Core() in ie_core.cpp, similar code as in the function getStaticPluginsRegistry() could be used as a fallback if plugins.xml is missing at runtime. Generally, we are open to modify the CMake or source code files accordingly. However, before programming anything we would like to discuss this idea first. So what do you think? Do you agree that this might be useful feature or does it even conflicts with your plans? Thanks for your time!

title: [Bug] Critical section not initialized. (Failed to allocate graph: MYRIAD device is not opened.)
author: SiegfriedIppischSecuriton
body: System information (version)  OpenVINO => 2022.2 af16ea1 Operating System / Platform => Windows 64 Bit Compiler => Visual Studio 2019 Problem classification: Debugging with Application Verifier / Windows critical sections Model name: person-detection-retail-0013  Detailed description We found some problems with an active Application Verifier while debugging an application which uses OpenVino. Our company is using this tool, but OpenVino triggers those checks too. This also makes it harder for us, to find other problems. Something is wrong with critical sections inside OpenVino. Those are not correctly used according to the Windows API. The Windows dokumentation says the following about critical sections:  Before the threads of the process can use it, initialize the critical section by using the InitializeCriticalSection or InitializeCriticalSectionAndSpinCount function.  and  Any thread of the process can use the DeleteCriticalSection function to release the system resources that are allocated when the critical section object is initialized. After this function is called, the critical section object cannot be used for synchronization. The problem occurred on multiple machines (with different driver versions, some just booted up, some on standby for a period of time to reuse). title: [RISCV] Discuss opprtunities to extend OpenVINO with RISCV support
author: vladimir-dudnik
body: Hello OpenVINO team, Thanks you guys for amazing work you are doing, we’d like to ask your opinion on opportunity to add OpenVINO support for RISCV CPU ISA to enable DL inference on this promising new architecture. As you probably know, RISCV committee has ratified some time ago vector extension v1.0 (kind of SIMD technology but vector length may vary at runtime). At the moment there are publicly available tools which enable development for this new arch (although, there is no CPU with RVV 1.0 hardware implementation available at the market yet but it is expected they may appear at this year or beginning of the next year). So, for now there is gcc and clang compilers capable to generate RVV 1.0 code and there is QEMU emulator, allowing functional testing of such code. Also, as we can see, there is some effort in community to bring up inference capabilities on RISCV architectures (https://github.com/tum-ei-eda/muriscv-nn, https://github.com/rvboards/ncnn and there are might be others). We think having OpenVINO API available for RISCV platforms would be beneficial for both OpenVINO and community. So, we have tried those compilers with OpenVINO code base and successfully build OpenVINO and CPU plugin (with minor cmake files adjustments to enable new toolchain). Obviously, when CPU plugin compiled for new CPU architecture, all x86 specific optimization turned off and only ngraph reference code is actually compiled. But this makes OpenVINO work on RISCV, we successfully passed OpenVINO conformance tests on RISCV QEMU (although performance of reference code is not good, expectable). That makes us think that ngraph reference code could be replaced one by one with RVV 1.0 optimized code, under conditional compilation, for example, allowing performance boost on RISCV CPUs. What is you guys vision on this? Do you think it make sense to bring RISCV support to OpenVINO and if so, what should be the best way to implement this? We also may need pay attention to the possibility for RISCV vendor specific extensions, in other words, RISCV committee ratified base RVV 1.0 ISA, which any RISCV CPU should be compatible with, and also allow vendor to extend RISCV ISA with some specific, optional extensions (for example DSP, or compressed instructions or whatever). It seems to support RISCV vendor adoption for OpenVINO we may need to think about some way to enable this kind of differentiation across CPU vendors. Something like specify not only 'CPU' as execution device, but also have ability to enable or disable some vendor extensions, to allow portability on application level through different RISCV implementations/platforms. Would be interesting to hear back your opinion on this Thanks

author: EdjeElectronics
body: System information (version)  OpenVINO=> 2022.2 Operating System / Platform => Windows 11 64 Bit Compiler => Python runtime installed using PyPI Problem classification => n/a  System devices:  i7-12700 CPU  (CPU) Intel UHD Graphic 770 iGPU  (GPU.0) Intel Arc A750 dGPU  (GPU.1)  Detailed description When a model is compiled in AUTO mode, the get_property method reports device priorities in the reverse order than what is stated in documentation. The Automatic Device Selection page states that devices are reported from high to low, and that the default priority order is dGPU, iGPU, VPU, and CPU. In my case, get_property reports CPU,GPU.0,CPU.1, which is the reverse of the expected order.  Steps to reproduce The problem can be reproduced by running the following Python code. I ran it on a machine with a CPU, iGPU, and dGPU installed. When the code below is run, it will report MULTI_DEVICE_PRIORITIES: CPU,GPU.0,GPU.1, which is reverse from the expected priority order. I also uploaded a notebook (forked from openvino_notebooks) that can be used to reproduce the problem: https://github.com/EdjeElectronics/openvino_notebooks/blob/main/notebooks/108-query-device/108-query-device.ipynb # Initialize OpenVINO from openvino.runtime import Core ie = Core()  # Download model base_model_dir = "model" model_name = "person-detection-0202" precision = "FP16" model_path = (     f"model/intel/{model_name}/{precision}/{model_name}.xml" ) download_command = f"omz_downloader " \                    f"--name {model_name} " \                    f"--precision {precision} " \                    f"--output_dir {base_model_dir} " \                    f"--cache_dir {base_model_dir}" ! $download_command  # Compile model in AUTO mode model = ie.read_model(model=model_path) compiled_model = ie.compile_model(model, "AUTO")  # Check MULTI_DEVICE_PRIORITIES property hint_priorities = compiled_model.get_property("MULTI_DEVICE_PRIORITIES") print('MULTI_DEVICE_PRIORITIES: %s' % hint_priorities)  Result: MULTI_DEVICE_PRIORITIES: CPU,GPU.0,GPU.1 If I compile the model in MULTI mode with the priority specified as GPU.1 , GPU.0 , CPU , then it does report the correct priority order. title: [Bug] Canceling transpositions are added when converting from TF
author: tazr
body: System information (version)  OpenVINO=> 2022.3 Operating System / Platform => Windows 64 Bit Compiler => N/A Problem classification => Model Conversion Framework: TensorFlow  Detailed description When converting a simple TF network and asking to switch to channel first layout, transpositions are added even in simple situations. This is not only a performance issue, but also a regression from 2021.4, where those transpositions where absent. Steps to reproduce Create this network from TF: import tensorflow as tf from tensorflow.tools.graph_transforms import TransformGraph  ph = tf.placeholder(dtype=tf.float32, shape=(1, 32, 32, 32, 2), name='input') y = tf.math.multiply(ph, 2, "output") with tf.Session() as sess:     g = tf.get_default_graph().as_graph_def()     g = TransformGraph(g, inputs=["input"], outputs=["output"], transforms=[])     tf.io.write_graph(g, ".", "test.pb", as_text=False) Convert using mo --use_new_frontend --input_model test.pb --input "input" --output "output" --layout "input(ndhwc->ncdhw),output(ndhwc->ncdhw)"  The resulting network has two canceling transpositions around the scalar multiplication:  Note that the same network converted with 2021.4 (which switched to channel-first by default) does not present this issue:  Issue submission checklist  [X ] I report the issue, it's not a question   [X ] I checked the problem with documentation, FAQ, open issues, Stack Overflow, etc and have not found solution   [X ] There is reproducer code and related data files: images, videos, models, etc.

title: [Bug] GRU layer  - failed conversion with TF 2.9.1
author: lebence
body: System information (version)  OpenVINO => 2022.2 Operating System / Platform => Ubuntu 20.04.5 LTS Compiler => Problem classification: Model Conversion Framework: TensorFlow  Detailed description When converting a simple TF network with GRU layer which was trained on TensorFlow 2.8 and saved into SavedModel format, there is no problem. I can convert my model easily without any error, with this code: mo --saved_model_dir /work/user/saved_model/my_model/ --input_shape [?,28,28] --output_dir /work/user/saved_model/vino   But when I change Tensorflow version to 2.9.1, and I train a TF network with GRU layer and save into SavedModel format, I get an error like this: [ ERROR ]  Cannot infer shapes or values for node "StatefulPartitionedCall/sequential/gru/PartitionedCall/TensorArrayV2_1". [ ERROR ]  Graph execution error:  Tensorflow type 21 not convertible to numpy dtype. [ ERROR ]   [ ERROR ]  It can happen due to bug in custom shape infer function <function tf_native_tf_node_infer at 0x7f6bf1b1c700>. [ ERROR ]  Or because the node inputs have incorrect values/shapes. [ ERROR ]  Or because input shapes are incorrect (embedded to the model or passed via --input_shape). [ ERROR ]  Run Model Optimizer with --log_level=DEBUG for more information. [ ERROR ]  Exception occurred during running replacer "REPLACEMENT_ID" (<class 'openvino.tools.mo.middle.PartialInfer.PartialInfer'>): Stopped shape/value propagation at "StatefulPartitionedCall/sequential/gru/PartitionedCall/TensorArrayV2_1" node.   For more information please refer to Model Optimizer FAQ, question #38. (https://docs.openvino.ai/latest/openvino_docs_MO_DG_prepare_model_Model_Optimizer_FAQ.html?question=38#question-38)   Steps to reproduce A short code, to reproduce this problem: import tensorflow as tf from tensorflow import keras from tensorflow.keras import layers  model = keras.Sequential() model.add(layers.GRU(64, input_shape=(28, 28))) model.add(layers.BatchNormalization()) model.add(layers.Dense(10)) print(model.summary())  mnist = keras.datasets.mnist (x_train, y_train), (x_test, y_test) = mnist.load_data() x_train, x_test = x_train/255.0, x_test/255.0 x_validate, y_validate = x_test[:-10], y_test[:-10] x_test, y_test = x_test[-10:], y_test[-10:]  model.compile(     loss=keras.losses.SparseCategoricalCrossentropy(from_logits=True),     optimizer="sgd",     metrics=["accuracy"], ) model.fit(     x_train, y_train, validation_data=(x_validate, y_validate), batch_size=64, epochs=5 ) model.save('saved_model/my_model') Then converting with this code mo --saved_model_dir /work/user/saved_model/my_model/ --input_shape [?,28,28] --output_dir /work/user/saved_model/vino  It works well with TF 2.8, but after the change TF to 2.9.1, I get an error, like above. Issue submission checklist   I report the issue, it's not a question    I checked the problem with documentation, FAQ, open issues, Stack Overflow, etc and have not found solution    There is reproducer code and related data files: images, videos, models, etc.

title: [Bug] Infinite recursion if find_package(OpenVINODeveloperPackage) is called twice
author: vinograd47
body: System information (version)  OpenVINO => 2022.3.0 and master Operating System / Platform => Ubuntu 22.04 CMake => 3.22.1 Problem classification: build scripts  Detailed description The issue can be reproduced with simple CMakeLists.txt file: cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.21) project(openvino_cmake_bug_repro) find_package(OpenVINODeveloperPackage REQUIRED) find_package(OpenVINODeveloperPackage REQUIRED) # intentional second call file(WRITE "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/fake.cpp" [=[ int main(int argc, const char* argv[]) {     return 0; } ]=]) add_executable(fake "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/fake.cpp") The second call of find_package(OpenVINODeveloperPackage REQUIRED) leads to infinite loop in CMake and the process is aborted by OS. In real life the above scenario might happen if one project uses another project as submodule and integrates it into single build tree and both projects use OpenVINO. After some investigation, I found that the issue happens due to message function overriding here. When the find_package(OpenVINODeveloperPackage REQUIRED) is called the second time, the function is overriden again, but _message call inside now calls the function itself, not the base implementation. It leads to infinite recursion, when OpenVINODeveloperPackageConfig.cmake tries to print OpenVINO version. Some thread about similar issues in CMake can be found here: https://cmake.org/pipermail/cmake/2011-March/043316.html The above example worked with OpenVINO 2022.2.0 because there ENABLE_ERROR_HIGHLIGHT option was set to OFF be default so the message was not overridden. In 2022.3.0 and master ENABLE_ERROR_HIGHLIGHT is turn on by default, which enables overriding and reveals this bug. Steps to reproduce Compile OpenVINO either with explicit -DENABLE_ERROR_HIGHLIGHT=ON option or without specifying it on 2022.3.0 or master. Then run CMake command with -DOpenVINODeveloperPackage_DIR=<path to OpenVINO build dir> on the above CMakeLists.txt example. Issue submission checklist   I report the issue, it's not a question  I checked the problem with documentation, FAQ, open issues, Stack Overflow, etc and have not found solution  There is reproducer code and related data files: images, videos, models, etc.

title: [Bug] remoteBlob cache machanism led the access to incorrect GEM buffer once the VASurfaceID repeated
author: joojler
body: System information (version)   OpenVINO=> 2021.4 Operating System / Platform => Ubuntu 18.04 Compiler => gcc Problem classification => inference failure  Detailed description  Inference will fail through remoteBlob based on VASurface under Linux once the VASurfaceID repeated. For example, when VASurfaceID == 100, it pass to IE for inference through remoteBlob, it succed. Later, we release this VASurfaceID, then allocate a new VA surface with the same VASurfaceID, then the inference will fail through remoteBlob. Did some debug, the problem is due to the cache mechnism of VASurface in remoteBlob. Both the OV 2021.4 and latest OV have similar problem. The logic will go into cache once the VASurfaceID and plane format are the same. But we do have some cases the VASurface is actually different even these attributes are the same. In some cases, i tried to disable the cache as the following, it works to do the inference. title: Request for i7-1260p in Openvino Benchmarks
author: justin-larking-pk
body: Currently the openvino benchmarks have the i9-12900k as an example of an alder lake processor for AI performance. This is compared to an 11th gen i7-1165g7 mobile cpu. Given the drastic difference in performance grade (i9 125w desktop chip versus a 28watt mobile chip) and the difference in iGPU, the comparison between 11th gen and alder lake isn't really present. It would be helpful to have a direct generation to generation comparison of the 1165g7 and the alder lake equivalent the 1260p. It would help user's of Openvino understand the affects of removing AVX-512 instructions from alder lake and what the addition of AVX-VNNI in alder lake has done to AI performance in these chips.

body: System information (version)  OpenVINO => Build number: 2022.3.0-9052-9752fafe8eb-releases/2022/3 Operating System / Platform => centos7 Compiler => gcc 4.8 Problem classification: Model Inference locally Framework: IR Model name: Quantized  custom tensorflow model to IR  Detailed description  I am currently using Go to call the Openvino C API and create several inference requests that I push to a channel in Go. While dealing with client requests, I obtain an idle inference request from the channel and use it to perform inference. After completing the inference, I send it back to the channel. At the beginning, stress testing is expected. However, after approximately 300 to 1000 requests, a TBB warning appears: TBB Warning: Exact exception propagation is requested by application but the linked library is built without support for it Additionally, the model's output size is unusual and different from what I expect. For instance, the input shape is (36, 37), where 36 is the batch size and 37 is the sequence length. Given that the model's hidden dimension is 146, the output size should be 36*37*146=194,472. Nevertheless, I am getting 138,116. title: [Bug] Compilation failure with THREADING=OMP and Visual Studio 2017
author: DmitryYurov
body: System information (version)  OpenVINO=> 2022.3 Operating System / Platform => Windows 11 64 Bit Compiler => Visual Studio 2017 Win64 (msvc 14.16.27023) Problem classification => Compilation failure  Detailed description Dear Team, I have tried to compile OpenVINO with OpenMP for multi-threading. However, I get numerous error messages from the compiler (see the attached screenshot). As far as I understand the problem is the obsolete OpenMP standard used by msvc (OpenMP 2.0).  With a newer compiler (e.g. MSVC 14.34.31933, Visual Studio 2022) I get lots of info C5002: Omp simd loop not vectorized due to reason '1200'  Steps to reproduce Just run compilation with the MSVC compiler and the OpenMP support as described in the documetation. In my case CMake has been run with the following flags: cmake -G "Visual Studio 15 2017 Win64" -DOpenCV_Dir=C:\\opencv\\4.5.3\\build -DTHREADING=OMP -DENABLE_INTEL_CPU=ON -DENABLE_INTEL_GPU=ON -DENABLE_INTEL_GNA=ON -DENABLE_TEMPLATE=OFF -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=release ../  I have attached CMakeCache.txt file for your information. title: [Bug] multithreaded application does not inference the openvino model on both NUMA nodes
author: ckumsta
body: System information (version)  OpenVINO=>2022.3 Operating System / Platform =>Windows Server 2022 64 bits Compiler =>Visual Studio 2019 Problem classification => C API V2.0 is not targeting the correct NUMA node during inference.  Detailed description The Goal:  running inferences from 8 threads dispatched across NUMA nodes (4 threads per node NUMA)  The How: I have an application in C# in which I created a wrapper for C API V2.0. The wrapper works, in appearance, properly. I can:  instantiate an ov_core_t object load and compile a model from disk and obtain an ov_compiled_model_t object create an ov_infer_request_t from the compiled_model get the input ov_tensor_t by index and fill it with images (images using Matrox Image Libray, because they use unmanage pointers too, it is relatively simple to remap parts of the tensor unmanaged data as Matrox image and fill the images with it) execute an inference using the infer function of ov_infer_request_t retrieve the ov_tensor_t from infer_request by index convert it back to images (batch used) And I get the absolute correct result from specific images as input, so far so good.  To optimize the process of our edge application (machine is running timed by a mechanical machine), the server is responsible of 2 vision systems (dual Intel Xeon Gold server), 1 per NUMA node. And to have a bit more latency per period (but less cores per thread), we use 4 running threads per node NUMA. To force the threads to be dispatched on the correct NUMA node, we wrap in C# the windows kernel functions: GetNumaNodeProcessorMaskEx, SetThreadGroupAffinity, etc etc. Before using OpenVINO, the image processing from Matrox (and IPP intel processing pack too) were correctly following the NUMA node association (the processing stays on the NUMA affinity of the thread). The Problem: When I started using OpenVINO, I did not realized immediatly the problem, but migrating more and more processing to UNet model, I realized that, differently from the image processing, all inferences are done on the first NUMA node. Even if the thread running the inference has the affinity set to the 2nd NUMA node. I use the Get/Set Property of OvCore with "AFFINITY" set to "NUMA", but it seems to do nothing. More strangely, I tried to Set the property "AFFINITY" to "CORE", and it read back "NUMA" ?? Steps to reproduce OpenVinoBugTest.zip I attached the zip of a complete solution demonstrating the problem. The solution is composed of:  shared library (all windows dll of openvino runtime, copied automatically to the exec folder) C# library that basically wrap the C API into Disposable C# objects Console application that demonstrate the problem:   doing busy jobs to watch the NUMA dispatching of threads on multithreaded workload during 10s, doing the openvino (1 per NUMA) in loop during 10s.  The execution on a dual CPU shows this (I select 1 node per display in the resource monitor, but watching the cores shows the same things and hovering the mouse over the graph display the NUMA node number):  We can see that first 10s of work is dispatched across both NUMA, but the second 10s of work is done on the first NUMA node only. One last thing, I tried to use the Get/SetProperty on the compiled_model, but it returns an "unknown exception" (17) no matter what I tried. Thank you very much for this wonderful DL framework. Issue submission checklist   I report the issue, it's not a question  I checked the problem with documentation, FAQ, open issues, Stack Overflow, etc and have not found solution  There is reproducer code and related data files: images, videos, models, etc.

title: [Bug] openvino does not work with other shells besides bash
author: Thodoris1999
body: Detailed description setupvars.sh as well as other shell scripts in this repository require the information of the location of the running script, which is unfortunately famously not posix standardized and each shell implementation provides its own workaround. This repository uses bash's workaround (BASH_SOURCE[0]), which silently does not work for any other shell implementation. Solutions  Create a complex function that gets the source path for each shell implementation Provide multiple setup scripts, e.g. setupvars.bash and setupvars.zsh (ROS approach) Use a user set environment variable (OPENVINO_HOME) and default to default path/symlink (/opt/intel/openvino), failing if it doesn't exist (nvidia approach)  Steps to reproduce Execute any of openvino's scripts with a non bash shell

title: Extend ONNX Frontend with `com.microsoft.Range` operator
author: p-wysocki
body: Context Neural networks are graphs consisting of nodes called operators. Each operator corresponds to a mathematical function, usually described in framework's documentation or an AI standard, such as ONNX. OpenVINO ONNX Frontend is a component responsible for working with ONNX graphs and requires implementation of different ONNX operators in order to use ONNX models. This task requires extending OpenVINO ONNX Frontend with com.microsoft.Range operator. Necessary help will be provided by ONNX Fronted team. Operator specification Operator details can be found in official ONNX Runtime docs. To do list  Create .hpp and .cpp files for com.microsoft.Range here Prepare an implementation of this operator in form of a function. It should be placed in opset 1 namespace. The implementation should be the same as standard ONNX Range operator Register the function in ops_bridge.cpp while keeping alphabetical order Create test model(s) in ONNX models directory. OpenVINO test infrastructure then converts prototxt files to ONNX models - you will use those models later in tests Add tests covering all use cases here  More details in adding operators to ONNX Frontend guide Resources  Guides on ONNX Frontend architecture and ONNX Frontend tests are also available Contribution guidelines can be found here You can also see a blog post on contributing to OpenVINO  Example PRs  #15076 #14936 #12510  Contact points @tomdol @mbencer @p-wysocki Don't hesitate to reach out, we're here to help!

body: I tried to asked this question in the Intel forum (that is referenced in the documentation), but it mangled my question text and then flagged it as spam. (https://community.intel.com/t5/Intel-Distribution-of-OpenVINO/MacOS-OpenVINO-built-what-next-and-more/m-p/1490656) [MacBook Pro 2014, MacOS 13.3.1, OpenVINO master, OpenCV 4.7.0] With an abstract understanding of deep learning and several of it's sub-fields and a NCS2, I now would like to tinker. So, I followed the OpenVINO build instructions for Intel MacOS (master branch) all the way up to step #4, and everything built/installed fine. With  OpenVINO installed on my computer (in /usr/local/OpenVINO) and my NCS2 plugged into my USB port, I believe I have everything needed to start using OpenVINO.  Thus I created my working folder with a virtualenv and decided to try the Hello Classification sample. Looking at the Hello Classification C++ Sample documentation page, it suggests to download the googlenet-v1 model. When I tried to do that, the omz_downloader script was not found. When I looked around my filesystem, I could not find the script in my OpenVINO install location but I did find it in the openvino workspace I cloned from github, under ./build/tools/openvino_dev/build/usr/local/bin/. However, when I run omz_downloader directly from that location, I got an error importlib.metadata.PackageNotFoundError: No package metadata was found for omz-tools. Prior to the model download step, the Hello Classification C++ Sample documentation page says to install openvino-dev[caffe], but I was reluctant to do this since I had just built everything and, to my mind, already have omz-tools. Whilst composing this question, I decided to try installing pip install openvino-dev anyway (python -m pip install openvino-dev[caffe] returned an error), thinking that maybe it would only download/install this particular part and any other dependencies that are needed. But, to my surprise, pip started installing openvino_dev-2022.3.0-9052-py3-none-any.whl. Sadly, this install failed! So now I seem to have two versions of OpenVINO on my system; the nightly I built and a broken 2022.3.0. I then attempted to install omz-tools itself, but pip complained:  pip install omz-tools  ERROR: Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement omz-tools (from versions: none)  ERROR: No matching distribution found for omz-tools  So, now I have several questions:  How do I remove all the files that were downloaded as a result of trying to install openvino-dev? How do I get the omz_downloader that I already have to work? Do I need to install, clone, build anything else? Could it be that I haven't installed everything I need, e.g. OMZ-Tools and other stuff, since I only did what was stated in the build guide.

title: ie_precision.hpp defines == operator but not !=
author: mjvh80
body: See                openvino/src/inference/include/ie/ie_precision.hpp                    Line 162       in       031f2cc                                                 bool operator==(const Precision& p) const noexcept {                     I just upgraded to Visual Studio 17.6 and in our codebase this header file generates error C2666 . We are using /std:c++latest. I believe it disregards the == operator because of a missing != operator. Indeed adding   bool operator!=(const Precision& p) const noexcept { return !(*this == p); } fixes our code. I'm not in a position to compile OpenVino itself at the moment, otherwise I'd have done a PR with this suggestion, or is there a reason not to add the != operator?

title: [Bug] Model Optimizer issues with rt_info "old_api_map_order"
author: Peter-McLean-Altera
body: System information (version)  OpenVINO Source => Runtime + GitHub (have both built and archive installs) OpenVINO Version => Version 2022.3 Operating System / Platform => SLES12/ SUSE12 Compiler => Cmake / Python 3.8.10 Problem classification: Model Conversio Device use: CPU Framework: TensorFlow2 Model name: Any model  Detailed description Model Optimizer insertion of old_api_map_order needs to be disabled automatically or have a flag to disable it when the user has explicitly transformed the model with --source-layout=...(nhwc) --target-layout=...(nchw). If the model is explicitly transformed to NCHW with the old front-end ahead of inference, the old_api_map_order is still in the model. This causes a (now) invalid transpose to be added to pre/post processing of the model. --use_new_frontend does NOT insert the old_api_map_order and does not appear to have this issue. I attempted to use MO_DISABLED_TRANSFORMS to disable the PreserveRuntimeInfo step, but it does not have an id. I attempted to use the module.name instead, but OpenVINO crashed. See steps and for the crash dump. Steps to reproduce Freeze a TF2 model in NHWC Attempt to disable rt_info old map order export MO_DISABLED_TRANSFORMS=openvino.tools.mo.middle.PreserveRuntimeInfo.PreserveRuntimeInfo Convert it with a similar command to this: mo --input=x[1 32 32 3]{f32} --source_layout=x(nhwc),model/conv1/BiasAdd(nhwc) --target_layout=x(nchw),model/conv1/BiasAdd(nchw) --output=model/conv1/BiasAdd --model_name=graph --input_model=identityconv_32x32_3_channels/inputs/frozen_graph.pb --output_dir=identityconv_32x32_3_channels/inputs/ --reverse_input_channels See example graph: identityconv_32x32_3_channels.zip The crash output [ ERROR ]  ------------------------------------------------- [ ERROR ]  ----------------- INTERNAL ERROR ---------------- [ ERROR ]  Unexpected exception happened. body: We convert one of the models from Caffe to OpenVino using MO. The approach had been to patch mo_caffe.py/caffe_pb.py, and deploy a FrontExtractorOp-derived class and Op-derived class. title: Segmentation fault when running `test_get_runtime_model` test
author: p-wysocki
body: Context One of our tests results in a segfault error when ran by itself. This is probably related to Model object destruction. This task regards finding the error and fixing it. This task allows for quick familiarization with the internals of OpenVINO Python API. Reproduction The issue is reproducible with the following command: python3 -m pytest tests/test_runtime/test_compiled_model.py::test_get_runtime_model -sv which needs to be ran from openvino/src/bindings/python. title: A Few Questions Regarding Post-training Quantization with Accuracy Control
author: edition3234
body: The official recommendation for the post-training quantization with accuracy control of OpenVINO models includes two methods: NNCF and Pot. I am wondering which one is better. It appears that the official side leans more towards NNCF, however, after gaining a rudimentary understanding of NNCF's quantization with accuracy control process, I discovered that it requires both a calibration dataset and a validation dataset. This seems different from Pot's approach, where it looks like an int8 model is being "retrained" based on the original model. NNCF seems to only decide whether to terminate the quantization process according to the validation function during the quantization. If I wish to pursue better quantization results, which method should I choose? I have just started learning about quantization and I don't fully understand NNCF and Pot. Please forgive me if there are any errors in my description.

body: System information (version)  OpenVINO Source => Runtime / GitHub OpenVINO Version => Version 2023.0.0 / Github Master Branch / tag 2023.0 Operating System / Platform => Ubuntu 18/20 Compiler => Cmake Problem classification: ov::Core Device use: CPU  Detailed description Actually, I don't have one problem. Very strange behavior of ov::Core. I read in the documentation that you recommend using the ov::Core object in a single instance for all models. I created an ov::Core object for each model and noticed that the model inference only uses one processor core for multiple asynchronous ov::InferRequest even though I used all possible options to compile the model. num_requests = 4; // For example model_ = core.compile_model(         model,         "CPU",         ov::hint::performance_mode(ov::hint::PerformanceMode::THROUGHPUT),         ov::streams::num(num_requests),         ov::inference_num_threads(num_requests),         ov::hint::num_requests(num_requests),         ov::hint::allow_auto_batching(false)); The thing was that the first model with the first initialization of ov::Core used num_requests processor cores, but after the destruction of the first model, I initialize the second model with the re-initialization of ov::Core, but this model already uses one processor core. But after I wrote static ov::Core (the object is now in a single instance), my problem was solved. Model inference started using num_requests of processor cores. I solved this problem, but that's not all. It turned out that due to the peculiarities of my model, I cannot create parallel requests in one model. In addition, I have another question about the options for compiling the model. I did not find a normal explanation in the documentation. title: OpenVINO can't be built in an environment that has an 'ambient' oneDNN installation
author: BillyONeal
body: The following configuration is broken: vcpkg install onednn vcpkg install openvino because openvino finds the onednn headers installed by onednn, rather than the forked copies it expects to use. It isn't clear to me as a vcpkg maintainer whether it is safe to devendor this and just use the onednn port. This will be a problem in any shared namespace scenario, like apt or dnf or vcpkg if they want both a onednn and openvino package. At least in vcpkg, OpenVINO claims to only support dynamic linking, where it is possible to not expose the internal forked copy of oneDNN, which means it is possible to always use the forked copy. However, OpenVINO refers to oneDNN headers with angle brackets (<onednn/dnnl.h>) which suggests 'any system provided copy of this header' rather than 'our specific fork'. Is there support for adding a ENABLE_SYSTEM_ONEDNN which would get OpenVINO out of this vendoring business? /cc @ilya-lavrenov who added openvino in microsoft/vcpkg#31671 and also seems to contribute directly here.

title: Extend ONNX Frontend with `BlackmanWindow`, `HammingWindow` and `HannWindow` operators
author: mbencer
body: Context Neural networks are graphs consisting of nodes called operators. Each operator corresponds to a mathematical function, usually described in framework's documentation or an AI standard, such as ONNX. OpenVINO ONNX Frontend is a component responsible for working with ONNX graphs and requires implementation of different ONNX operators in order to use ONNX models. This task requires extending OpenVINO ONNX Frontend with BlackmanWindow, HammingWindow and HannWindow operators. Necessary help will be provided by ONNX Fronted team. Operator specification Operator details can be found in ONNX Operators. Todo list  Create .hpp and .cpp files for *Windows here Prepare an implementation of this operator in form of a function. It should be placed in opset 1 namespace. Register the function in ops_bridge.cpp while keeping alphabetical order Create test model(s) in ONNX models directory. OpenVINO test infrastructure then converts prototxt files to ONNX models - you will use those models later in tests Add tests covering all use cases here  More details in adding operators to ONNX Frontend guide Resources  Guides on ONNX Frontend architecture and ONNX Frontend tests are also available Contribution guidelines can be found here You can also see a blog post on contributing to OpenVINO  Example PRs  #15076 #14936 #12510  Tips In ONNX specification example code, you can find numpy implementation which can be a good reference. BlackmanWindow # periodic window size = np.int32(10) a0 = 0.42 a1 = -0.5 a2 = 0.08 y = a0 y += a1 * np.cos(2 * 3.1415 * np.arange(0, size, 1, dtype=np.float32) / size) y += a2 * np.cos(4 * 3.1415 * np.arange(0, size, 1, dtype=np.float32) / size)  # symmetric window size = np.int32(10) a0 = 0.42 a1 = -0.5 a2 = 0.08 y = a0 y += a1 * np.cos(     2 * 3.1415 * np.arange(0, size, 1, dtype=np.float32) / (size - 1) ) y += a2 * np.cos(     4 * 3.1415 * np.arange(0, size, 1, dtype=np.float32) / (size - 1) )  HammingWindow # periodic window size = np.int32(10) a0 = 25 / 46 a1 = 1 - a0 y = a0 - a1 * np.cos(     2 * 3.1415 * np.arange(0, size, 1, dtype=np.float32) / size )  #symmetric window size = np.int32(10) a0 = 25 / 46 a1 = 1 - a0 y = a0 - a1 * np.cos(     2 * 3.1415 * np.arange(0, size, 1, dtype=np.float32) / (size - 1) )  HannWindow # periodic window size = np.int32(10) a0 = 0.5 a1 = 0.5 y = a0 - a1 * np.cos(     2 * 3.1415 * np.arange(0, size, 1, dtype=np.float32) / size )  # symmetric window size = np.int32(10) a0 = 0.5 a1 = 0.5 y = a0 - a1 * np.cos(     2 * 3.1415 * np.arange(0, size, 1, dtype=np.float32) / (size - 1) )  Note that OV equivalant of numpy.arange can be OV Range op Contact points @mbencer @p-wysocki Don't hesitate to reach out, we're here to help!

title: Evaluate Profile-Guided Optimization (PGO)
author: zamazan4ik
body: Hi! Recently I checked Profile-Guided Optimization (PGO) improvements on multiple projects. The results are here. LLVM-related results are here. Since PGO showed measurable improvements in compiler-like loads (CPython, Clang, Clangd, clang-format, GCC, Rustc, etc.) I think it could be useful to check PGO on OpenVino as well. We need to perform PGO benchmarks on OpenVino. And if it shows improvements - add a note about possible improvements in OpenVino performance with PGO. Providing an easier way (e.g. a build option) to build scripts with PGO can be useful for the end-users too. Maybe testing Post-Link Optimization techniques (like LLVM BOLT from Facebook) would be interesting too but I recommend starting from the usual PGO. I think the good starting point here could be recompiling 3rd parties with PGO (that's usually a good thing to do if possible). Another possible piece of code, that highly-likely (according to my guess) can be well-optimized with PGO is frontend. If you have better ideas - feel free to correct me!

title: Align `openvino.compile_model` and `openvino.Core.compile_model` functions
author: p-wysocki
body: Context There are two namespaces from which you can call a compile_model function:  openvino.compile_model The code for it can be found under https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino/blob/master/src/bindings/python/src/openvino/runtime/ie_api.py#L600-L610 openvino.Core.compile_model The code for it can be found under https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino/blob/master/src/bindings/python/src/openvino/runtime/ie_api.py#L495-L544  Currently, you can only give model_path argument to openvino.compile_model, which makes its behavior different from openvino.Core.compile_model, which can take three arguments. The goal of this task is to align the functions. What needs to be done?  Align the function behavior This can be done by changing the code for openvino.compile_model from  def compile_model(model_path: Union[str, Path]) -> CompiledModel: to something along the lines of def compile_model(     self,     model: Union[Model, str, Path],     device_name: Optional[str] = “AUTO”,     config: Optional[dict] = None, ) -> CompiledModel:  Add tests for openvino.compiled_model covering the new functionality Create a Pull Request  Resources  Contribution guide How to extend OpenVINO Python API How to test OpenVINO Python API Blog post on contributing to OpenVINO  Contact points @p-wysocki @jiwaszki @akuporos Don't hesitate to reach out, we're here to help! title: Add a clear error message when creating an empty `Constant`
author: p-wysocki
body: Context Current Constant implementation does not allow for creating empty Constants: https://docs.openvino.ai/2023.0/openvino_docs_ops_infrastructure_Constant_1.html Trying to do so results in a cryptic error message: IndexError: index 0 is out of bounds for axis 0 with size 0 What needs to be done?  Add a clear error message for the user trying to create an empty Constant This can be done in either Python wrapper: https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino/blob/master/src/bindings/python/src/openvino/runtime/opset1/ops.py#L334-L347 Or in C++ to Python binding: https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino/blob/master/src/bindings/python/src/pyopenvino/graph/ops/constant.cpp  It's up to you to decide where the error message implementation will be a good fit.   Make sure the error message appears This can be done either manually or by writing a test.   Create a Pull Request   Resources  Contribution guide How to extend OpenVINO Python API How to test OpenVINO Python API Blog post on contributing to OpenVINO  Contact points @p-wysocki @jiwaszki @akuporos Don't hesitate to reach out, we're here to help! title: [Feature Request]: Improve the ov_core_read_model_from_memory API Definition in OpenVINO Library
author: sdcb
body: Request Description The current OpenVINO library API ov_core_read_model_from_memory seems to have a design issue. Specifically, the model_str parameter, which appears to be a string, actually points to the model file in memory. Internally, it is then converted into a string for processing. This leads to a problem where if the model file includes a null character ('\0'), the read-in model size will be smaller than the actual size. Conversely, if the model file does not contain a null character, it will inevitably cause a memory error. /**  * @brief Reads models from IR / ONNX / PDPD / TF / TFLite formats.  * @ingroup ov_core_c_api  * @param core A pointer to the ie_core_t instance.  * @param model_str String with a model in IR / ONNX / PDPD / TF / TFLite format.  * @param weights Shared pointer to a constant tensor with weights.  * @param model A pointer to the newly created model.  * Reading ONNX / PDPD / TF / TFLite models does not support loading weights from the @p weights tensors.  * @note Created model object shares the weights with the @p weights object.  * Thus, do not create @p weights on temporary data that can be freed later, since the model  * constant data will point to an invalid memory.  * @return Status code of the operation: OK(0) for success.  */ OPENVINO_C_API(ov_status_e) ov_core_read_model_from_memory(const ov_core_t* core,                                const char* model_str,                                const ov_tensor_t* weights,                                ov_model_t** model); I propose to modify the API by renaming the model_str parameter to model_data, and adding a new integer parameter model_data_size after it, to accurately represent the memory size of model_data. OPENVINO_C_API(ov_status_e) ov_core_read_model_from_memory(const ov_core_t* core,                                const char* model_data,                                const int model_data_size,                                const ov_tensor_t* weights,                                ov_model_t** model); Feature Use Case This proposed change would prevent potential memory errors and inaccurate model size readings that can occur if model files contain or lack null characters. It would increase the robustness of the API, making it more reliable and easier to use for developers. This improvement could also potentially increase the efficiency of model loading operations, as it provides clearer information about the memory size required for the operation. Issue submission checklist   The feature request or improvement must be related to OpenVINO

title: [Good First Issue]: Compile OpenVINO on macOS with Xcode cmake generator
labels: good first issue;category: build;platform: arm;platform: macOS;no_stale
author: ilya-lavrenov
body: Context OpenVINO is a cross platform product, which can be built with different compilers, their versions. But different compilers and cmake generators can slightly adjust their option, so the product compilation emits warnings. The proper way is to align compiler options, so the product compilation become less OS / compiler / cmake generator dependent. E.g. if MSVC on Windows often emits signed / unsigned types conversion, we need to find similar option for Clang / GCC and enable by default and fix warnings. With this task, you can understand simple OpenVINO data structures, get an experience with working with compiler flags, making a portable code base. What needs to be done? Run cmake with: cmake -G Xcode -DCMAKE_COMPILE_WARNING_AS_ERROR=ON -S <openvino source> -B <build dir>  And build with: cmake --build . --parallel --config Release -- -IDEBuildingContinueBuildingAfterErrors=YES  And fix all compilation errors, adjust cmake flags where it's needed. title: [Good First Issue]: Refactor `torchvision` preprocessing converter into Python `singledispatch`
author: p-wysocki
body: Context We strive to keep our code as clean as possible - one of the ways to do it is to use advanced Python features. One of them is singledispatch method, which you can read more about here. This feature has been introduced in Python 3.8, so we were hesitant to use it, and in the end used a workaround - we download singledispatchmethod from PyPI as a dependency, for Python 3.7 only (we support a range of Python versions). Right now we are in the process of dropping Python 3.7 support, which means we can use singledispatch freely. This task regards refactoring some code in our torchvision preprocessing converter to use singledispatch feature. What needs to be done? The task regards addressing these two TODO comments:  https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino/blob/master/src/bindings/python/src/openvino/preprocess/torchvision/torchvision_preprocessing.py#L50 https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino/blob/master/src/bindings/python/src/openvino/preprocess/torchvision/torchvision_preprocessing.py#L70  The functions need to have "overloads" for different types of inputs. Right now it's being done by simple if conditions, but it should be done with singledispatch. An example implementation of singledispatch can be found in our data dispatcher. title: Extend ONNX Frontend with `Shape-15` operator
author: mitruska
body: Context Neural networks are graphs consisting of nodes called operators. Each operator corresponds to a mathematical function, usually described in framework's documentation or an AI standard, such as ONNX. OpenVINO ONNX Frontend is a component responsible for working with ONNX graphs and requires implementation of different ONNX operators in order to use ONNX models. This task requires extending OpenVINO ONNX Frontend with Shape-15 (ONNX Shape operator since ONNX Opset 15). ONNX Shape operator has been extended with additional "start, end" attributes, what should be reflected in the conversion logic. Currently those attributes are ignored by ONNX FE, and ONNX Shape is converted directly to ov::ShapeOf, but it can be supported at the ONNX FE conversion step, with additional ov::Slice layer. Necessary help will be provided by ONNX Fronted team. Operator specification Operator details can be found in ONNX Operators. Todo list  Update .hpp and .cpp files: /openvino/src/frontends/onnx/frontend/src/op/shape.hpp /openvino/src/frontends/onnx/frontend/src/op/shape.cpp Prepare an implementation of this operator in form of a function. It should be placed in set_15 namespace. Register the next version of the Shape operator: REGISTER_OPERATOR("Shape", 15, shape); in ops_bridge.cpp while keeping alphabetical order Create ONNX Shape-15 test model(s) in ONNX models directory. OpenVINO test infrastructure then converts prototxt files to ONNX models - you will use those models later in tests. Double check the ONNX opset version of the model that should be at least 15. Add tests covering all use cases here  More details in adding operators to ONNX Frontend guide Resources  Contribution guide - start here! title: [Good First Issue]: Automate the Good First Issues board - "Assigned" column
author: p-wysocki
body: Context We have recently switched to managing the Good First Issues using GitHub Projects. Another step towards easier management is automating the board, so the tasks move between columns without having to manually drag them. The board can be found under https://github.com/orgs/openvinotoolkit/projects/3 The board has been partially automated using the default GitHub Workflows:  Newly added issues with label "good first issue" are automatically added to "Contributors needed" column When an issue is closed, it automatically moves to the "Closed" column  However, the columns "Assigned" and "In review" cannot be automated using the default GitHub Workflows. This task regards automating the "Assigned" column. What needs to be done? title: [Good First Issue]: Support TruncateMod operation for TensorFlow models
author: rkazants
body: Context OpenVINO component responsible for support of TensorFlow models is called as TensorFlow Frontend (TF FE). TF FE converts a model represented in TensorFlow opset to a model in OpenVINO opset. In order to infer TensorFlow models with TruncateMod operation by OpenVINO, TF FE needs to be extended with this operation support. What needs to be done? For TruncateMod operation support, you need to add the corresponding loader into TF FE op directory and to register it into the dictionary of Loaders. One loader is responsible for conversion (or decomposition) of one type of TensorFlow operation.
